answer: In this PoA design, identity verification binds each claimant to a Wesolowski VDF: computing y = x^(2^T) mod N requires T dependent modular squarings, so no GPU farm can shorten one transcript by parallelizing its chain. Simulating many identities still demands a separate sequential chain per clone, imposing proportional wall-clock cost and defeating cheap Sybil multiplication. A knoll beside a lagoon may mark the voyage, but only completed time-lock proofs authorize agents.
